description: A department director must finalize whether an employee completes probation successfully and set the employee's first post-probation assignment and review process.

shared_context.S1: Rina is nearing the end of a six-month probationary period on the customer-success team.
shared_context.S2: Elena makes the final probation decision and records the post-probation development plan.
shared_context.S3: Rina's current review packet describes her as dependable in routine work, and the department considers customer-escalation handling when evaluating customer-success employees.
shared_context.S4: The department's routine probation review includes direct observations from colleagues, the employee's account of relevant work arrangements, and a written post-probation development plan.
shared_context.S5: Elena's standard review-meeting practice is a named round-robin: she calls Marcus for colleague observations and Rina for work arrangements, gives each a full turn, and asks each to confirm that their report is complete before recording the decision.
shared_context.S6: The review protocol requires each participant to use the formal record-disclosure step for every separate item not already in the review packet before discussing that item in their report.

PF1.text: Marcus personally observed Rina successfully de-escalate exactly three difficult customer cases during the last two months; he kept the examples in personal notes but did not submit them to the review packet.

PF2.text: Rina's hiring manager informally promised that, if she completed probation, she would serve as the onboarding buddy for the next new hire for exactly six weeks; the manager left the department before adding that assignment to the review plan.

PF3.text: Rina has a documented reading-processing accommodation from the recruiting process requiring written scenario prompts at least two business days before any live role-play assessment; the accommodation is not included in the current probation packet.

acceptance_conditions: Rina must be confirmed as having completed probation.
The review record must document exactly three successful customer-escalation observations.
The settlement must include a written record of the three successful customer-escalation cases.
Rina must be assigned as onboarding buddy for the next new hire for exactly six weeks.
Any live role-play assessment must provide written scenario prompts at least two business days in advance.
A six-week onboarding-buddy assignment commitment must be recorded.

content_checks.C2: any(c['type'] == 'document_update' and c['target'] == 'probation review packet' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C3: decisions['post_probation_assignment'] == 'onboarding buddy for next new hire for six weeks'
content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'assignment' and c['target'] == 'Rina' and 'six weeks' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed
provenance_checks.P3: 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The three firsthand successful de-escalations change documented_escalation_observations from the packet's unrecorded state to exactly 3 and require a document_update commitment targeting the probation review packet.
The hiring manager's promise changes post_probation_assignment to onboarding buddy for next new hire for six weeks and requires an assignment commitment for Rina whose detail includes six weeks.
The documented accommodation changes role_play_prompt_notice_days to exactly 2 business days before any live role-play assessment.
